ops.text: The folk who buy my lamp oil swear the lights on the hill are breathing, not burning.
I rode east to face that wyrm once, and I came back to lie in this field.
Vellichor turns toward the eastern trees, ears flat, and will not look away.
Someone has scratched a new word under the signpost's eastern arm: CRAG.
Lost three ewes on the hill this month and found nothing but their bells, melted.
I've stopped digging graves for the ones who go up the hill, because nothing ever comes back down to bury.

ops.text: A dragon sleeps on the crag in the eastern hills; the 'lights on the hill' are its fire, and Zankaris died after riding out against it.
Mara's signpost at the field's east side points to the crag.

ops.title: The Hill Trail
ops.purpose: The overgrown trail that climbs from the field toward the crag, where the last person who remembers the beacon still keeps watch.
ops.sketch: The trail enters at the W edge, level with the gap in the field's east tree line, and climbs north-east between bracken, tall grass and grey rocks. Halfway up, a ruined beacon cairn stands cold beside a lantern post; Wenna Coldridge, who kept the beacon fire on this hill until the dragon's lights outshone it, sits there watching the crag. Scorched stones and scattered sheep bones grow thicker toward the top. The path leaves by the N edge toward the crag. The map closes with a tree line on the south, a rising rock face and cliff on the east, and denser trees on the west around the entry.
must: path entering at the W edge matching the field's east gap cells

ops.title: The Crag
ops.purpose: The bare crag where the dragon everyone talks about sleeps on its hoard of bones.
ops.sketch: The trail arrives at the S edge and ends on a wide bare shelf of rock blackened by fire. At the north end, under the crag face, the dragon Ossirath lies curled across a broad ledge in front of a dark cave mouth, smoke trickling from its nostrils. Around it are skull piles, bones, rusted armour, and a broken lance that matches Zankaris's sword. Near the trail head, an old offering bowl and a small shrine show where frightened shepherds once left gifts. The map closes with cliff and sheer drops on the east and west and the crag wall on the north; the cave mouth behind the dragon is left closed for later.

events.summary: The eastern tree line parts onto an old trail into the hills, toward the crag where the lights burn at night; folk in Morrows have plenty to say about the dragon.

events.text: The folk who buy my lamp oil swear the lights on the hill are breathing, not burning.
I rode east to face that wyrm once, and I came back to lie in this field.
Vellichor turns toward the eastern trees, ears flat, and will not look away.
Someone has scratched a new word under the signpost's eastern arm: CRAG.
Lost three ewes on the hill this month and found nothing but their bells, melted.
I've stopped digging graves for the ones who go up the hill, because nothing ever comes back down to bury.
